title: Wires in a magnetic field: practice
search_keywords: magnetic induction, current-carrying wire, F = IlB sin theta, permeability of free space, motor, loudspeaker, past papers
ican: I can explain the forces on the coil of a motor.

cloze.title: Say it the exam way
cloze.text:
The magnetic induction near a long straight wire is [[directly|inversely]] proportional to the current. It is [[inversely|directly]] proportional to the distance from the wire. The constant μ₀ is the permeability of [[free space|the wire]].

The force on a wire is F = IlB sin θ, where θ is the angle between the wire and the [[field|force]]. The force is greatest when the wire is at [[90°|0°]] to the field. When the current is [[parallel|perpendicular]] to the field, there is no force. Two parallel wires carrying current in the same direction [[attract|repel]]. The unit of force per unit length is [[N m⁻¹|N m]].

paper2.alt: A loudspeaker consists of a coil of wire, attached to a cone, which is free to move in the field produced by a permanent magnet. Figure 10A shows the magnet, the coil, the cone and the AC signal. The coil and cone oscillate when an AC signal is supplied to the coil. The oscillation can be modelled as simple harmonic motion. (b) An AC signal supplied to the coil has a frequency of 55.1 Hz. (i) Show that the angular frequency of the coil and cone is 346 rad s⁻¹. 2 marks. (ii) The amplitude of the oscillation is 8.24 mm. Calculate the maximum acceleration of the coil and cone. 3 marks. (c) A magnetic force acts on the coil when there is current in the coil. Data sheet: mass of coil and cone 0.177 kg; magnetic induction 1.10 T; length of conductor in coil 21.8 m. By considering the magnetic force acting on the coil, determine the minimum current required to produce the maximum acceleration of the coil and cone. 4 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2023 Question 10(b)(ii) and (c). (b)(ii) 3 marks: a = (−)ω²y (1); a max = (−)346² × 8.24 × 10⁻³ (1); a max = (−)986 m s⁻² (1). Accept 990, 986.5, 986.46. (c) 4 marks: (F =) IlB = ma (1, 1); I × 21.8 × 1.10 = 0.177 × 986 (1); I = 7.28 A (1). Accept 7.3, 7.278, 7.2778. Or consistent with (b).

paper2.lead: Part (b)(ii) is simple harmonic motion. It gives the maximum acceleration that (c) needs.

paper2.alt: A student designs an experiment to determine the permeability of free space, μ₀, by measuring the magnetic induction around a current carrying wire. Figure 14A shows the wire and a magnetic sensor connected to a laptop. The front of the magnetic sensor is 0.010 m from the wire. (b) The current in the wire is varied and the magnetic induction is measured. Figure 14B is a graph of magnetic field strength in microtesla against current in amperes, from 0 to 1.6 A, with a best-fit line labelled y = 19.4x + 2.8. (i) Using information from the graph, determine a value for μ₀. 3 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2023 Question 14(b)(i), 3 marks: gradient = 19.4 × 10⁻⁶ (1); B = μ₀I ÷ 2πr; 19.4 × 10⁻⁶ = μ₀ ÷ (2π × 0.010) (1); μ₀ = 1.2 × 10⁻⁶ H m⁻¹ (1). Accept 1, 1.22, 1.219. Or consistent with a gradient calculated using two points on the line.

paper2.alt: A model electric motor consists of a rotor, which is free to rotate about an axis perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field, as shown in Figure 15A: a coil of wire PQRS between a north pole and a south pole. The length of the wire along side PQ is 45 mm. The magnetic induction between the poles is 44 mT. The current in the coil is 0.56 A. (b) The rotor now rotates 90 degrees clockwise to the position shown in Figure 15B. (i) On Figure 15C, show the direction of the forces acting on sides PQ and RS of the rotor. 1 mark. (c) The rotor is modified so that there are now two perpendicular coils of wire, as shown in Figure 15D. Explain why this modification improves the operation of the model electric motor. 1 mark.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2026 Question 15(b)(i) and (c). (b)(i) 1 mark: a diagram with a force arrow on side PQ and an opposite force arrow on side RS. Both arrows are required. (c) 1 mark: there is always a (component of) force perpendicular (to the axis of rotation). Also accepted: the torque is never zero (when there is current in the coil).

paper2.lead: Part (a) was done in class. The stem is here because (b) and (c) need it.

paper2.alt: A student measures the magnetic induction at a distance r from a long straight current carrying wire using the apparatus shown in Figure 14: a wire, a magnetic sensor in a protective casing, and a magnetic induction meter. The data are: distance from wire r = 0.10 m; magnetic induction B = 5.0 microtesla. (a) Use the data to calculate the current I in the wire. 3 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2016 Question 14(a), 3 marks: B = μ₀I ÷ 2πr (1); 5 × 10⁻⁶ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ × I ÷ (2π × 0.1) (1); I = 2.5 A (1). Accept 3, 2.50, 2.500.

errors: No force when the current is parallel to B.
